title: Visual Identity
intro: A white peak on a gradient tile, locked to a two-tone wordmark set as one name. Every mark on this page is rendered live by the same components the site itself ships — not a screenshot — so what you see here is exactly what visitors get.

rationale.title: Why it looks like this
rationale.lead: B2B software for businesses of every size: appointments, quotes, signatures, change requests. Trusted, precise, intelligent — enterprise-ready without feeling cold. Every decision carries a meaning tied to that.

items.body: An upward triangle with a notch cut from its base — three readings at once: the apex of a summit (growth, the ambition of the businesses you serve), a checkmark-adjacent silhouette (approval — quotes signed, appointments confirmed), and an F/S ligature reduced to pure geometry. Solid fill = certainty; nothing decorative.

A rounded square is the most "software" of shapes — an app icon by construction. It carries the brand gradient, and the peak cut from it stays white at every size: the one contrast pairing that never has to be checked.

Periwinkle #5A68C4 into plum #8A4270, at 45°, always running bottom-left to top-right. Two colors instead of one corporate flat fill — movement and range, without giving up the discipline of a fixed axis.

"Francisco" in iris, "Solis" in ink — one name, two words made legible without a space or hyphen. The color split does the job punctuation would, which mirrors the product philosophy: structure without friction.
A geometric sans with slightly humanist curves — precise letterforms (enterprise-ready) that avoid the coldness of stricter grotesques (not overly corporate).
Ink #1E1E1E for authority, one accent for action, near-white surfaces — the restraint itself signals "we handle serious business documents."

lockup.title: Horizontal lockup
lockup.body: The mark and the wordmark travel together. FranciscoSolis is one name: no space, no hyphen, and no line break between the words. Use it for the website header, docs, and email signatures.
lockup.note: On dark surfaces "Francisco" lightens to iris-300 and "Solis" goes paper. Everywhere else it stays iris-500 over ink — iris-500 on ink only reaches 2.8:1, so it never appears there.

vertical.title: Vertical lockup
vertical.body: For square placements and splash screens, where the horizontal lockup would have to set too small to stay legible.

mark.title: The mark alone
mark.body: Used for app icons, avatars, and favicons. The tile's corners are rounded at 20% of its edge — the same ratio at every size, so the curve reads identically in a 16 px favicon and a 1024 px export. It never sets below 16 px — under that the peak's shoulders close up and the tile's radius starts eating the artwork.
mark.sizes_label: 16, 24, 32, 64 px, the square tile and the circle avatar
mark.shapes_note: Upload the square tile anywhere the platform rounds or crops the icon itself — app stores, social avatars, iOS home screens. Rounding it twice is what leaves the corners looking clipped. The circle is for platforms that force a circular crop and offer no square option.
mark.mono_body: For single-color contexts — print, engraving, watermarks. Reach for these instead of recoloring the tile or flattening the gradient.

color.title: Color tokens
color.body: The palette is fixed. Click any token to copy its value.
color.gradient_note: The gradient always runs periwinkle (bottom-left) → plum (top-right) at 45°. Never reverse or re-angle it, and never apply it to the wordmark text.

uses.brand/gradient: Tile fill and hero surfaces only

contrast.title: Contrast guide
contrast.body: Measured against WCAG 2.1 for normal text. Anything not listed here has not been cleared.

spacing.title: Spacing guide
spacing.body: Screen values at 96 dpi, where 1 px = 0.2646 mm. Clear space and the tile gap scale proportionally with the mark.

rules.clear_space: Clear space, all sides (½ mark height @ 64 px)
rules.tile_gap: Tile → wordmark gap (0.28 × mark height @ 64 px)

type.title: Typography
type.body: The wordmark is Sora SemiBold (600) at −2% letter-spacing. Sora is the wordmark face only — the product UI runs on Inter and does not need to match.

clear_space.title: Clear space
clear_space.body: Keep clear space equal to half the mark's height on every side of any lockup. Where a container's own padding already meets that — as the site header's does — don't add it a second time.
clear_space.label: half the mark's height

rules.title: Do and don't
rules.body: The short version of everything above.
do_items: Keep the peak white on the tile — always
Use the mono marks in single-color contexts
Hold clear space: half the mark's height, all sides
Use the supplied files — never retype or redraw
dont_items: Don't stretch, squash, or rotate the mark
Don't recolor the tile or substitute a flat fill for the gradient
Don't reverse or re-angle the gradient
Don't apply the gradient to the wordmark text
Don't place the mark on low-contrast backgrounds
Don't add a space or hyphen, or change the casing of the name

code.title: Using it in code
code.body: In this site, compose the lockup from the React components rather than linking the SVG files. The reference SVGs set the wordmark as SVG text in Sora, which resolves against locally installed fonts only — anywhere Sora isn't installed the wordmark silently falls back to a system sans and loses its shape. The components draw the mark inline and set the wordmark as real text in the webfont, so it stays crisp, selectable, and readable to screen readers.

assets.title: Assets
assets.body: SVG is the source of truth, PNG ships at 4× for universal use, WEBP is the web-optimized export. Use these for handoff — design tools, documents, and third parties.
assets.note: Lockup SVGs require Sora to be installed on the machine rendering them; the PNG and WEBP exports have the type baked in.

uses.mark_square: Full-bleed, no rounding — for platforms that round or crop the icon themselves
uses.favicons: Favicon and PWA icon set, in px
